tldr: For a binary \(2^2\) randomized factorial experiment, the full observed uptake law yields a complete closed-form sharp set for the constant-complier focal main effect under the same focal-factor monotonicity, common least-profile, focal weak-exclusion, and pathwise outcome-exclusion restrictions used by the binary anchor specialization.  Pathwise outcomes and full response maps induce exactly the same \((p,\delta_k)\) class.  A CC/NC/NN transport decomposition reduces compatibility to cell capacities and one shared exclusion budget, and the two unknown success masses form a rectangle intersected with an \(L^1\)-distance budget.  This supplies the exact two-sided full-law compatibility test, constructive elimination, sharp endpoints, equality tests, and endpoint regimes absent from the checked anchor, whose Proposition 2 uses focal margins and whose explicit \(K=2\) full-law specialization is one-sided.  The genuinely two-sided five-type law has focal-margin interval \([1/4,1/2]\) and full-law set \(\{1/2\}\); a compact two-type law gives a second strict example, from \([-1,0]\) to \(\{-1\}\).  For arbitrary \(K\), the secondary reachable-support formulation remains exact, with promised-compatible endpoint evaluation fixed-parameter tractable in reachable-support size.
